name: 15h cosine retrieval
title: Cosine similarity ranks chunks by direction rather than length
subtitle: Toy embeddings with three coordinates: returns, item condition, delivery

steps.caption: An embedding model turns each text into a vector. Here each coordinate is a made-up topic score: returns, item condition, delivery. The query asks about returning a damaged item.
Lengths come first. Length is the square root of the sum of squares, so c1 = (4, 3, 0) has length √(16 + 9) = 5, c2 has length 1 and c3 = (0, 0, 2) has length 2. The query already has length 1.
Dot product with c1: multiply matching coordinates and add. 0.6×4 + 0.8×3 + 0×0 = 4.8.
Dot product with c2: multiply matching coordinates and add. 0.6×0 + 0.8×0.6 + 0×0.8 = 0.48.
Dot product with c3: multiply matching coordinates and add. 0.6×0 + 0.8×0 + 0×2 = 0.
The raw dot product gives c1 a score of 4.8 partly because c1 is a long vector. Doubling a vector doubles its dot product without changing what it is about.
Cosine divides by both lengths: 4.8 / (1 × 5) = 0.96. Only the angle between the two arrows is left.
Cosine divides by both lengths: 0.48 / (1 × 1) = 0.48. Only the angle between the two arrows is left.
Cosine divides by both lengths: 0 / (1 × 2) = 0.00. Only the angle between the two arrows is left.
Ranking by cosine gives c1 (0.96), c2 (0.48), c3 (0). With k = 2 the retriever passes c1 and c2 to the model. If c1 is the chunk that answers the question, recall@2 for this query is 1.
